subject: MAP: CrossOrg POC — IP safelist, org seed, API key handoff & VPC peering
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Dana Park <dana@crossorg.com>, CloudOps Team <ops@crossorg.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-03T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: MAP: CrossOrg POC — IP safelist, org seed, API key handoff & VPC peering

Hi Dana / CloudOps,

Thanks again for the time today — as promised, attaching a one-sheet MAP (CR-2047_MAP_v1.1.xlsx) that breaks the POC environment setup into clear ownerable steps. High-level ask from CrossOrg for the hosted evaluation is: can we get an org seed, short-lived API keys, and either an IP allowlist or VPC peeringstitch in the next 7 business days so their devs can run synthetic and real traffic?

Top-line items I want to confirm with you here so we can lock dates:
- Org create and tenant seed (env name, admin user list) — Redwood action: create sandbox tenant and invite CrossOrg admins.
- API key issuance (ephemeral key + instructions) — Redwood action: grant scoped eval key with 48h TTL.
- IP safelist + CIDR for quick test traffic — CrossOrg provides CIDR(s).
- VPC peering template if you prefer peering instead of IP safelist — we provided a YAML template (vpc_peering_template.yaml) for their infra team.

If you can confirm preferred connectivity (safelist vs peering) and the point people for CrossOrg infra (ops + network), we’ll schedule a 30-min technical cutover window.

Next steps I propose:
1) Dana confirm connectivity choice + CIDRs or Peering SNI by EOD Wednesday (5/5).
2) Redwood to create org seed and pre-generate API keys for test accounts by Thursday (5/6) pending confirmation.
3) If peering chosen, CloudOps and our infra ops do a VPC template run during a 30-min window on Friday.

Thanks —
Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
m: +1 415-555-0123
A: Redwood Inference, San Francisco

Attachments: CR-2047_MAP_v1.1.xlsx, vpc_peering_template.yaml (stubs)

From: Dana Park <dana@crossorg.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: CloudOps Team <ops@crossorg.com>, Rajiv Menon <rajiv@crossorg.com>
Date: 2027-05-03T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP: CrossOrg POC — IP safelist, org seed, API key handoff & VPC peering

Thanks Marcus — appreciate the clear breakdown. Quick answers from our side:
- We prefer starting with IP safelist for the first 48–72 hours to validate behavior, then move to VPC peering if we see sustained load.
- CIDR blocks: 34.120.0.0/22 and 34.120.4.0/22 (we can tighten later).
- Point people: Rajiv (rajiv@crossorg.com) for infra, and CloudOps alias for implementation.

Can you confirm the exact TTL and rate-limits on the ephemeral keys? Also, if you can pre-provision the sandbox org and add my admin account (dana@crossorg.com), that’ll speed verification.

Dana
Dana Park
Director, Product — CrossOrg

On Mon, May 3, 2027 at 09:12 AM Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai> wrote:
> (See above)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-04T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: RE: MAP: CrossOrg POC — IP safelist, org seed, API key handoff & VPC peering

Marcus — quick infra notes to coordinate once Dana confirms: 

1) Org seed: I’ll create a sandbox tenant named crossorg-eval-2027 and invite dana@crossorg.com + rajiv@crossorg.com as admins. Will record tenant ID and posted link in the Jira ticket.

2) API keys: We can generate scoped test keys with a 48-hour TTL and token-scoped rate limit 50rpm by default for the POC. If CrossOrg needs higher throughput for a burst test, we can set an alternate key with 500rpm for a 2-hour window (we should capture approval).

3) IP safelist: Ops needs the CIDRs in the exact format to push to the firewall: 34.120.0.0/22, 34.120.4.0/22. Once they’re pushed, there’s a 15-minute propagation window.

4) VPC peering: our template requires a 10.0.4.0/16 range for Redwood side; CrossOrg will need to provide their peer CIDR and acceptance key. Olga — can you prep a short-runbook for the Friday peering window if Dana converts?

I’ll draft the email that contains the ephemeral key instructions + security notes (don’t share keys in public chat, rotate keys after validation, reuse of keys prohibited).

-Neha

On Mon, May 3, 2027 at 11:04 AM Dana Park <dana@crossorg.com> wrote:
> (See above)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Dana Park <dana@crossorg.com>, CloudOps Team <ops@crossorg.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-05T16:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP: CrossOrg POC — IP safelist, org seed, API key handoff & VPC peering

Great — thanks for the fast reply, Dana. Confirming actions and cadence: 

- CrossOrg decision: start with IP safelist (34.120.0.0/22, 34.120.4.0/22).
- Redwood actions this week:
   * Today (5/5) by 18:00 PT — create org crossorg-eval-2027 and invite Dana & Rajiv.
   * Tomorrow (5/6) 09:00 PT — post ephemeral API key instructions and generate two test keys (48h TTL, and one burst key 2h @ 500rpm locked behind approval).
   * Thursday (5/7) — if CrossOrg requests peering, we’ll execute the vpc_peering_template.yaml during a pre-scheduled 30-min window; Olga will lead.

Rajiv / ops team — when you have a minute, please confirm you received the invite and that your infra can push the two CIDRs to your firewall. If you prefer, we can do the safelist push on our side and you can pull-verify.

I’ll attach the 1-page MAP into the Jira ticket and flag the calendar invites for the two windows. We’ll also include a short eval checklist so the CrossOrg devs can validate sample requests and measure latency.

Marcus

Attachments referenced: CR-2047_MAP_v1.1.xlsx (short MAP with owners & dates), vpc_peering_template.yaml (template; only used if you opt for peering).
